summary.en: Danish prince elected King of the Hellenes in 1863. His reign of fifty years saw the kingdom gain the Ionian Islands, Thessaly, Epirus, Macedonia and Crete. He was assassinated in Thessaloniki five months after its capture.

body_html.en:
The National Assembly chose Prince William of Denmark after the British candidate, Prince Alfred, was ruled out by the Powers. He arrived in October 1863; Britain's cession of the Ionian Islands was the settlement's dowry.

George governed through parliament rather than around it, and after 1875 accepted the principle that the prime minister must command a majority. He lived to see the Balkan Wars double the size of his kingdom. On 18 March 1913, walking without a guard in newly captured Thessaloniki, he was shot dead by a man with no political motive anyone could establish.

title.en: The Union of the Ionian Islands
